card: Clamps negative and NaN timeout parameters to zero in the mining IPC methods waitTipChanged and waitNext, removing an assertion that aborts debug builds. An external IPC client passing negative or NaN values currently triggers an Assume crash on debug builds and bypasses comparison checks in release builds to cause wait delays. The author reproduced the crash on debug builds with a timeout of -1.0, though notes no known client currently sends negative or NaN timeouts.
evidence: PR description: 'On debug builds, a negative or NaN timeout fails this check and aborts the node. I reproduced this with a timeout of -1.0.'

Author acknowledges no known client currently exhibits this: 'I'm not aware of any client that sends these values (sv2-tp, for example, requires an interval of at least one second), so this is hardening against bad input from ipc clients.'
problem: External IPC callers can pass negative or NaN timeout values to mining interface methods. In debug builds, negative or NaN values trigger an Assume assertion failure that crashes the node; in release builds, NaN values bypass clamping checks and cause unexpected delays when passed to wait_until.

risk.why: A mistake in timeout handling could cause IPC mining template calls to return immediately or wait indefinitely, disrupting external mining services.

scope_notes: The patch is small (+25/-5 across 4 files) and updates IPC interface handling and tests.
summary: Clamps negative and NaN timeout values to zero in the mining IPC interface methods waitTipChanged and waitNext. It removes an Assume assertion in waitTipChanged that aborts debug builds when a negative timeout is received, and adds functional test coverage.
uncertainties: The patch was omitted from the prompt, so the exact clamping implementation cannot be directly verified.
